pageCache.text:
Love, Hope, Perseverance, Respect, Responsibility
Blandford St Mary
Welcome to Blandford St Mary Church of England Primary School. I feel immensely proud to be the Headteacher of this wonderful one-form entry school where children truly are at the heart of everything we do.
We offer excellent standards of care, guidance and support and a high-quality learning environment to support all learners equally. The school upholds an ethos of high expectations which provides children with challenging opportunities where children acquire skills, knowledge and confidence that can be applied to all future learning experiences. These opportunities encourage respect, self-belief, excellence and enjoyment and prepare our pupils for the next stage of their education.

Year 5 are spreading the message that everyone is special, everyone is valued and everyone has something wonderful to offer. pageCache.text:
Christian Distinctiveness
Collective Worship
Collective Worship at our school is highly valued, with time set apart each day for the whole school community to gather together in a time of reflection, to have the opportunity to engage with their own spirituality, to learn about the Biblical teachings and further explore our school's vision and values. During these special times, the school is still, quiet and respectful. For an overview of our collective worships please refer to the files at the bottom of this page.
All worship begins with the lighting of our three candles and saying our welcoming words.
Harvest
This year, we have once again held a whole school harvest service to celebrate God's goodness in creation. During our harvest service, we thanked God for providing us with the resources to grow such a wide variety of delicious foods in our world. We also took the opportunity to thank the people who grow and harvest our foods - mums and dads in their allotments and the farmers in their fields.
Our school community collected food items to donate to the Blandford Foodbank. As you can see from the picture below, our families, once again, have been extremely generous in their donations to help others. Thank you.
Christingle
In our Christingle Service we heard that Jesus said, Christians are ‘the light of the world’ (Matthew 5.14-16) and that they should love the world like God does.
Christians are called to be a shining light for those people who are in dark places and Christians are called to love everyone, particularly if they are having a bad time.
No matter what we believe, we can all be shining lights and show love to those who are in need of it.
Spirituality at Blandford St Mary
At Blandford St Mary CE Primary School, we believe that spiritual development is a fundamental aspect of children's personal growth and well-being. It is not limited to any faith or religious belief, but is something that can be experienced through learning, play, and everyday life.
Spirituality is not something we can see — it is something we feel inside. It shapes how we understand ourselves, how we relate to others, how we experience the world, and how we explore the mystery and wonder of life.
We aim for all children to develop holistically so that they become happy, fulfilled, spiritually aware, and socially and emotionally engaged.
For further detail, please refer to our Spirituality Definition and our Spirituality Policy at the bottom of this section.

pageCache.pageTitle: Blandford St Mary CE Primary School and Nursery - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision and Values
At Blandford St Mary, our vision statement of 'Knowing we are loved, we learn and grow to be the best that we can be,' is expressed through our Biblical underpinning, ‘Let all that you do be done in Love.’ – 1 Corinthians 16-14. The simplicity of this theological vision makes it accessible to everyone—whether they are of Christian faith or not. It reflects a loving and compassionate focus, rooted in God’s love for us, which is evident throughout our school. In every aspect of school life, we seek to reflect God’s love in all we do.
This verse speaks to the heart of Christian living—placing love at the centre of all our actions. Love, in the biblical sense, is not merely an emotion but a commitment to kindness, patience, respect, forgiveness, and compassion. These qualities align directly with our school's Christian values or Love, Hope, Perseverance, Respect and Responsibility, and underpin our aspiration to nurture a community where every child and adult is known, valued, and loved.
Choosing this verse as our foundation sets a clear, accessible standard for children and adults alike. It reminds us that our motivations matter—that how we speak, act, learn, correct, support, and celebrate should always be rooted in love. This promotes a school environment where relationships flourish, children feel safe, and learning is joyful.
Value tokens are awarded to the children for expressing our Christian values through their everyday actions. Children vocalise how proud they are to receive values tokens and add their personal leaf to our values tree —a growing symbol of how love shapes our community.
All relationships in school are consistently built on love. There is a strong emphasis on mutual respect and genuine care, and this is evident in the positive, trusting relationships we have with parents and the wider community. Parents comment on how welcomed and supported they feel, and staff work in close partnership with families to ensure the best outcomes for every child.
Even though our Biblical underpinning, “Let all that you do be done in love,” can be seen on all our walls, it is not just a display. It truly is the heartbeat of our school. It informs our ethos, drives our actions, and shapes the kind of community we are striving to be: a place where love is seen, heard, and felt in everything we do.
Values leaves are awarded to children for living out our Christian values and showing these in school. Alongside this, children receive values tokens, which they place in our tubes in the entrance hall – a visual way of seeing our values in action.
This DSAT bear was presented to our school In January 2020 in celebration of our school joining the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust. This bear is a symbol of the care and friendship our school will experience as part of the Trust.
The children and staff were asked to name the bear!
Amare was the name chosen by the staff and children as “amare” means “to love” in Latin, but it is also said to mean “the Lord said” in Hebrew.

pageCache.text:
Sport Premium
Impact and Sustainability
The Sport Premium funding has had a significant influence on our whole school development. We have taken huge steps forward in promoting education, school sport and active lifestyles through this funding. A key factor in our planning of the sport premium budget has been ‘variety’, where we believe that all pupils should be provided with a varied, active and engaging curriculum in Sport. For example pupils now have opportunities in: orienteering, golf, sailing, wind-surfing, paddle boarding.
Staff training has identified areas for development and provided opportunities for staff to expand their knowledge in order to offer high quality PE lessons. Teaching Assistants have had bespoke CPD in Invasion Games and Striking and Fielding Games. All staff had CPD in Invasion Games and Gymnastics.
We have adapted from a mainly single sports provider to gain a range of opportunities for both children and staff. We have been ever present at all of the local sporting events which we are invited to. Our development of intra-school provision has influenced our playtimes. Over the past 12 months we have had no significant behaviour issues. Children look forward to their sessions on the Astro, Basketball zone or Fitness Centre.
Sports Funding
All primary schools in England receive a grant from the Department for Education. All schools in receipt of the grant are obliged to publish on their websites details of how they spend their PE and sport grant. This must include details about the impact this funding has on pupils’ PE and sport participation and attainment.
Further information is available by clicking in the links below.

Starting Reception
Starting Reception is an exciting milestone for both children and families. To help make this transition as smooth and positive as possible, we have gathered together a range of useful information and resources to support you and your child as they prepare to begin school life at Blandford St Mary Primary School.
We recommend exploring the Starting Reception – Early Years Toolkit, which offers a range of helpful activities, videos and guidance for families with children starting Reception.

pageCache.text:
Governance
We are proud to support our school as part of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust. Working alongside school leaders, the ASEC (our local tier of governance) helps ensure every child receives a high-quality education in a safe, caring and inclusive environment. We provide strategic challenge and support, monitor the school's progress and wellbeing, and promote its Christian vision and values. Our governors are volunteers drawn from the local community who are committed to helping the school flourish. We value the partnership between families, staff and governors and look forward to supporting the continued success of our school.
We are members of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust and the governance of the Trust belongs to the main DSAT Board. Our Scheme of Delegation also includes our Constitution and Terms of Reference. You can find details of the Trust Board and details of our governance structure by visiting the Trustees page.
The Clerk to the ASEC can be contacted by emailing: jallen@dsat.org.uk

Curriculum
At Blandford St Mary Primary School and Nursery, we work closely as one team to ensure that every child enjoys a rich, engaging and progressive journey through our curriculum, from their very first experiences in Little Birch and throughout their time at school. Our carefully planned curriculum builds on children’s knowledge, skills and experiences at each stage, creating strong foundations for future learning. Through collaboration, shared expectations and a deep understanding of our children, staff ensure that learning is connected, purposeful and appropriately challenging, enabling every child to develop confidence, curiosity and independence from an early age. We are committed to giving every child the very best start, equipping them with the knowledge, skills and positive attitudes they need to flourish as they progress through their primary education and beyond.

SEND
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
At Blandford St Mary Primary School, we use the definitions of Special Educational Needs (SEN) and disability outlined in the SEND Code of Practice (2015) and the Equality Act (2010).
Special Educational Needs
The SEND Code of Practice states:
"A child or young person has special educational needs if they have a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for them. A learning difficulty or disability is a significantly greater difficulty with learning than the majority of others of the same age. Special educational provision means educational or training provision that is additional to, or different from, that made generally for others of the same age in a mainstream setting in England."
The Equality Act 2010 defines a disability as:
"A physical or mental impairment which has a long-term and substantial adverse effect on a person's ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities."
Many children and young people with SEN may also have a disability as defined by the Equality Act 2010.
SEND Contact Information
Mrs Katie Drake is the Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator (SENDCo) at Blandford St Mary Primary School.
Email: sen@blandfordstmary.dsat.org.uk
The designated governor for SEND is Mrs Sarah Granados.
How We Support Pupils with SEND
Support will always include Quality First Teaching and may also include:
Additional literacy support
Additional numeracy support
Small group interventions
Support from the School Nurse
Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA) provision
One-to-one interventions
Visual Impairment Team support

Curriculum
At Blandford St Mary Primary School, we provide a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum that builds carefully on the knowledge, understanding and skills of all children, regardless of their starting points. Our curriculum meets the statutory requirements of the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework and the Primary National Curriculum (2014), while also offering rich experiences and opportunities that respond to the learning and developmental needs of our pupils.
As a school community, our curriculum is driven by our core values of Aspiration, Communication and Curiosity. These principles underpin our curriculum intent and guide our approach to teaching and learning, encouraging children to aim high, express themselves confidently and develop a lifelong love of learning. At Blandford St Mary Primary School, we are committed to supporting the development of the whole child, ensuring that academic achievement sits alongside personal growth, wellbeing and character development.
